full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionRespiratory viruses are major global pathogens because of their high transmissibility, ability to persist on surfaces, and potential to cause epidemics. Although airborne spread is the principal route of transmission, contaminated surfaces and shared objects represent important secondary reservoirs, particularly in communal and healthcare settings (Haas et al., 2023). This risk is especially pronounced in hospitals, daycare centers, and pediatric wards, where high-touch items are frequently reused without adequate decontamination between uses. To address this challenge, the present study examines the virucidal efficacy of non-thermal plasma (NTP), a dry, low-temperature disinfection technology, against four clinically relevant respiratory viruses with distinct biological properties: severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A virus (IAV), human rhinovirus (HRV), and human adenovirus (HAdV).SARS-CoV-2, an enveloped RNA virus, demonstrated remarkable epidemic potential during the recent pandemic (Fathizadeh et al., 2020). Although enveloped viruses are generally more susceptible to disinfectants, the prolonged stability of SARS-CoV-2 on surfaces and in aerosols underscores the need for reliable decontamination strategies (van Doremalen et al., 2020). Moreover, repeated outbreaks caused by related coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV, indicate that members of the Coronaviridae family are likely to remain relevant targets for future infection-control efforts (Civljak et al., 2020). IAV, another enveloped RNA virus, is a frequent cause of seasonal and localized epidemic outbreaks (Moa et al., 2001). Its persistence in aerosols, low infectious dose, and rapid antigenic evolution make it a continuing public health challenge and a priority target for improved disinfection approaches (Tellier, 2009; Wu et al., 2020).Non-enveloped viruses such as HRV and HAdV present additional challenges because of their marked environmental stability. HRV, a ubiquitous cause of respiratory tract infections, can remain infectious on surfaces and is difficult to eliminate from porous substrates because of its small particle size and structural resilience. HAdV is among the most resistant human viruses; its robust non-enveloped capsid and stable DNA genome make it particularly difficult to inactivate and therefore a useful indicator organism for evaluating disinfection technologies (Lion, 2014; Lion, 2019). Although adenovirus infections are often self-limiting in immunocompetent individuals, they can cause severe outbreaks in crowded settings and life-threatening disease in immunocompromised patients (Hiwarkar et al., 2018; Sammons et al., 2019).Standard decontamination approaches, including ultraviolet (UV) irradiation, gamma irradiation, and chemical disinfectants, are often poorly suited to sensitive materials. UV light has limited penetration, and its efficacy is substantially reduced by surface irregularities and shadowing (Deng et al., 2020; Derraik et al., 2020; Kayani et al., 2021; Mills et al., 2018). Gamma irradiation requires specialized infrastructure and may compromise material integrity (Derraik et al., 2020; Rutala et al., 2023). Conventional liquid disinfectants are incompatible with many moisture- or heat-sensitive items and may leave residues that are undesirable in pediatric or clinical environments (Rutala et al., 2023; Obrova et al., 2022).These limitations are particularly relevant for porous, soft, and absorbent materials such as plush toys, foam rubber, paper, and cardboard. Plush toys, often composed of polyester or cotton fibers with sponge-like inner structures, can trap microbes deep within multiple layers. Foam rubber, including polyurethane-based materials used in cushions, child seating, and packaging, readily absorbs fluids and resists complete drying. Paper and cardboard, which are common in books, educational toys, and packaging, may deform or degrade when exposed to heat or moisture (Rutala et al., 2023; Scholtz et al., 2023).Such materials are ubiquitous in pediatric environments, where tactile play, frequent handling, and hand-to-mouth behavior increase the risk of contamination and transmission. Children are also more susceptible to infection because their immune systems are still developing, and viral shedding may be greater and more prolonged than in adults (Costa et al., 2012; Prendergast et al., 2012). Consistent with this vulnerability, contaminated toys and shared supplies in hospitals and daycare centers have repeatedly been implicated in outbreaks of influenza and adenovirus infections among children (Bearden and Casanova, 2016).Against this background, NTP has emerged as a promising alternative disinfection technology. NTP is a partially ionized gas generated at room temperature and atmospheric pressure that contains reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS), UV photons, ions, and electrons (Scholtz et al., 2023; Graves, 2012). In contrast to conventional methods, NTP provides dry, non-thermal, and non-wetting disinfection, making it particularly suitable for soft and porous materials that would otherwise need to be discarded after contamination (Obrova et al., 2022; Scholtz et al., 2023). Previous studies have shown that NTP can inactivate SARS-CoV-2, IAV, HRV, and HAdV on parafilm, P3 R filter material, foam, and other filter-based substrates, with dose-dependent reductions in viral titers (Obrova et al., 2022; Bouazizi et al., 2024).A further advance has been the development of portable, affordable, 3D-printed plasma devices optimized for microbiocidal performance and improved surface coverage of irregular materials such as plush toys and layered foams. By promoting deeper penetration and more uniform exposure, these devices may enable the safe reuse of items in pediatric care while reducing waste, lowering transmission risk, and extending the availability of essential resources during periods of shortage, including pandemics (Obrova et al., 2022; Scholtz et al., 2023; Bouazizi et al., 2024; Klenivskyi et al., 2024). 2.1Non-thermal plasma (NTP) deviceNTP was generated by point-to-ring corona discharge in a device whose operating parameters (discharge power: 0.7 W, voltage: 6–8 kV, current: 100–150 μA) were specifically optimized for enhanced antimicrobial and virucidal efficacy. The optimization process is described in detail in our previous works (Bouazizi et al., 2024; Klenivskyi et al., 2024), which involved systematic variation of the interelectrode distance (0–8 mm) and discharge current (50–500 μA) and assessment of the bactericidal effect on Escherichia coli. The selected parameters represent the optimal balance between maximum antimicrobial activity and stable, spark-free discharge operation.Further details of the NTP device and the concentrations of long-lived plasma-generated species (NO2, N2O, O3, and H2O2) measured under identical operating conditions were described in our previous study (Bouazizi et al., 2024). 2.4Virus strains and cell linesThe following virus strains and cell lines were used: SARS-CoV-2 (hCoV-19/Czech Republic/NRL_6632_2/2020) (Bouazizi et al., 2024; Vankova et al., 2020), propagated in Vero E6 cells (ATCC CRL-1586) in DMEM containing Pen/Strep and 10% FBS; IAV H1N1/California/07/2009 (Diagnostic Hybrids, Athens, OH, United States), propagated in MDCK cells (ATCC CCL-34) in influenza growth medium (IGM) consisting of DMEM supplemented with Pen/Strep, 0.2% BSA, 1 mM HEPES, 13.6 mM L-glutamine, 42 mg/L DEAE-dextran, and 1 mg/L TPCK-trypsin; HAdV species C/type 2 (ATCC VR-846), propagated in A549 cells (DSMZ ACC107) in DMEM containing 10% FBS and Pen/Strep; and HRV A/type 2 (ATCC VR-482), propagated in HeLa Ohio cells (both a kind gift from G. papers.full_text_excerpt: IntroductionHeat- and moisture-sensitive porous materials such as plush toys, paper products, and foam are widely used in pediatric and healthcare environments but cannot be decontaminated by conventional liquid disinfectants, heat, or UV-based methods. Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising approach for disinfecting such materials without compromising their integrity.MethodsIn this study, we assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber.ResultsMaterial characterization by SEM and XPS demonstrated only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage following NTP exposure. Several virus-material combinations exhibited biphasic inactivation kinetics characterized by an initial rapid decline followed by a slower phase of inactivation.DiscussionThese findings support that NTP could be an effective, residue-free, and material-preserving method for inactivating a broad spectrum of respiratory viruses on porous substrates incompatible with conventional disinfection. This creates a need for alternative dry, non-thermal technologies. Across all substrates, NTP treatment produced time-dependent reductions in viral infectivity. Maximum reductions ranged from 5.5–6.3 log10 for SARS-CoV-2, 6.3–7.1 log10 for IAV, 4.0–5.9 log10 for HAdV, and 2.7–5.0 log10 for HRV, depending on the virus-material combination. Enveloped viruses (SARS-CoV-2 and IAV) were inactivated more rapidly than the non-enveloped viruses HAdV and HRV, although all viruses were reduced to nearly or completely undetectable levels after 30–60 min of treatment. papers.title_original: Non-thermal plasma efficiently decontaminates sensitive materials from respiratory viruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of non-thermal plasma (NTP) in decontaminating sensitive materials from respiratory viruses, addressing the challenge of disinfecting heat- and moisture-sensitive substrates commonly used in healthcare and pediatric environments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A virus (IAV), human adenovirus (HAdV), and human rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber.
analysis.methods: Non-thermal plasma (NTP) was generated with specific parameters (discharge power: 0.7 W, voltage: 6–8 kV, current: 100–150 μA) optimized for antimicrobial and virucidal efficacy. Material morphology and surface structure were analyzed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS).
analysis.main_results: SEM imaging showed no substantial morphological alterations in paper after NTP exposure, minor fiber coiling in plush fabric, and no structural damage in foam rubber. XPS analysis indicated mild surface oxidation without significant structural changes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that NTP is an efficient and material-compatible method for inactivating a broad spectrum of human respiratory viruses on porous, heat- and moisture-sensitive substrates, demonstrating its potential as a novel decontamination approach.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that NTP could be a valuable tool for decontaminating sensitive materials in healthcare settings, offering an alternative to conventional methods that may damage these materials.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not provide detailed information on the specific viral strains tested or the exact mechanisms of NTP inactivating viruses, which may limit the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the focus on material characterization rather than direct viral inactivation measurements.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the use of non-thermal plasma (NTP) for decontaminating sensitive materials from respiratory viruses, particularly human adenoviruses. The research addresses the challenge of disinfecting heat- and moisture-sensitive substrates like paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber, which cannot be effectively treated with conventional methods. The methods involved generating NTP with optimized parameters and assessing material damage using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Results showed minimal structural changes in the materials after NTP exposure, indicating its compatibility with these substrates. The authors interpret that NTP is an efficient method for inactivating a broad range of respiratory viruses, offering a novel approach for decontamination in healthcare environments. However, the study lacks detailed information on specific viral strains and mechanisms of action, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估非热等离子体(NTP)在净化敏感材料免受呼吸道病毒污染方面的有效性,解决对医疗保健和儿科环境中常用的热敏和湿敏基材进行消毒的挑战。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了原型 NTP 装置对四种临床相关呼吸道病毒——SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感病毒 (IAV)、人腺病毒 (HAdV) 和人鼻病毒 (HRV)——应用于纸张、毛绒织物和泡沫橡胶的杀病毒功效。
analysis_zh.methods: 非热等离子体 (NTP) 是通过优化抗菌和杀病毒功效的特定参数(放电功率:0.7 W,电压:6-8 kV,电流:100-150 μA)生成的。使用扫描电子显微镜 (SEM) 和 X 射线光电子能谱 (XPS) 分析材料形态和表面结构。
analysis_zh.main_results: SEM 成像显示,在 NTP 暴露后,纸张没有明显的形态变化,毛绒织物中有轻微的纤维卷曲,泡沫橡胶没有结构损坏。XPS 分析表明表面轻度氧化,没有显着的结构变化。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,NTP 是一种高效且材料兼容的方法,可灭活多孔、热和湿度敏感基材上的多种人类呼吸道病毒,证明了其作为新型净化方法的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,NTP 可能是医疗机构中敏感材料净化的宝贵工具,为可能损坏这些材料的传统方法提供了替代方案。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究没有提供有关测试的特定病毒株或 NTP 灭活病毒的确切机制的详细信息,这可能会限制结果的普遍性。由于关注的是材料表征而不是直接的病毒灭活测量,因此证据是中等的。

papers.full_text: BackgroundCOVID-19-related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) disrupted the circulation of many respiratory pathogens. After these measures were lifted, pediatric respiratory pathogen activity may have changed in pathogen-specific ways. However, laboratory-based evidence using continuous multi-year data, interrupted time-series analysis, and contextual factors such as meteorology, air quality, and school calendars remains limited.MethodsWe conducted a single-center retrospective laboratory study of pediatric and neonatal inpatients aged 0–14 years with clinically diagnosed lower respiratory tract infection from January 2021 to December 2025. After 7-day deduplication within the same child, 20,250 throat-swab testing records were included. The NPI period was January 2021–December 2022, and the post-NPI period was January 2023–December 2025. Thirteen pathogen categories were analyzed using period comparisons, interrupted time-series models, and multivariable logistic regression incorporating meteorological factors, air quality index, and school-term status.ResultsOverall positivity was higher in the post-NPI period than in the NPI period (75.4% vs. 58.8%), and co-detection was also higher in the post-NPI period (15.2% vs. 6.0%). Pathogen-specific interrupted time-series analysis showed heterogeneous patterns: human adenovirus showed a robust immediate level decrease (−13.00 percentage points; 95% CI, −20.13 to −5.87; FDR-adjusted P = 0.005), whereas human rhinovirus showed a significant positive trend change after the January 2023 interruption (+1.07 percentage points per month; 95% CI, 0.63–1.50; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001), with a positive post-NPI slope (+0.64 percentage points per month). Higher temperature was associated with lower positivity of human respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, and influenza B virus, but higher positivity of human parainfluenza virus and human bocavirus. School-term status was associated with higher human rhinovirus positivity (aOR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.34–2.52; FDR-adjusted P = 0.002).ConclusionThe NPI and post-NPI periods showed distinct and heterogeneous temporal patterns in pediatric respiratory pathogen detection. These findings support integrated hospital-based laboratory surveillance centered on pathogen-specific temporal trends and interpreted alongside demographic, multi-pathogen, environmental, school-calendar, and longer-term temporal context. 2Materials and methods2.1Study design, setting, and data sourceThis single-center, laboratory-based retrospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Clinical Laboratory at Beijing Anzhen Nanchong Hospital of Capital Medical University and Nanchong Central Hospital, located in Nanchong, Sichuan Province, China. The hospital is a tertiary general hospital and clinical teaching hospital that receives patients from Nanchong and surrounding areas. Pediatric respiratory pathogen nucleic acid testing records from January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2025, were extracted from the laboratory information system. Throughout the study period, the data-collecting hospital, clinical laboratory, and respiratory pathogen testing framework remained consistent. Annual pediatric and neonatal inpatient volumes from 2021 to 2025 were obtained from hospital administrative records and used to calculate the number of respiratory pathogen testing records per 100 inpatient admissions as a contextual measure of testing volume across study periods.2.2Study populationEligible testing records were from pediatric or neonatal inpatients aged 0–14 years with a clinician-recorded diagnosis of lower respiratory tract infection on the laboratory test request. These patients underwent routine 13-target multiplex respiratory pathogen testing between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2025. Testing was ordered by clinicians according to the child's clinical presentation and diagnostic needs. Throat swabs were collected for respiratory pathogen nucleic acid testing. Records were required to contain complete information on sex, age, application date, and pathogen detection results. Outpatient and emergency department records were not included. Throughout the study period, the source wards, age range, eligibility criteria, and specimen type remained consistent.A total of 21,132 original identification records were initially available. After preliminary data cleaning, variable harmonization, and verification of key fields, 20,296 preliminary testing records were retained. To reduce the influence of repeated short-term testing from the same child, 7-day deduplication was performed using medical record numbers. For each child, testing records were ordered chronologically by application time; when multiple respiratory pathogen tests occurred within a 7-day window, only the first record was retained, whereas a test performed more than 7 days after the previously retained record was considered a new testing event. After deduplication, 46 short-term duplicate records were removed, leaving 20,250 testing records for the main analysis, including 6,490 records from the NPI period and 13,760 from the post-NPI period. The final dataset covered 60 consecutive months from January 2021 to December 2025. The overall study design, data-cleaning process, 7-day deduplication procedure, study-period classification, and analytical workflow are summarized in Figure 1.Figure 1Study design, data cleaning, and analytical workflow. The figure shows the data source, exclusion process, 7-day deduplication, study-period classification, and analytical framework. The NPI period was defined as January 2021 to December 2022, and the post-NPI period was defined as January 2023 to December 2025. During 7-day deduplication, only the first testing record from the same child within a 7-day window was retained. NPI, non-pharmaceutical intervention.Flowchart of study record selection and analysis. A total of 21,132 pediatric 13-pathogen respiratory nucleic acid testing records were screened; 836 records were excluded during data cleaning, leaving 20,296 preliminary records. After excluding 46 non-first repeat tests within 7 days, 20,250 records remained. These were classified into the NPI period (January 2021-December 2022; n = 6,490) and post-NPI period (January 2023–December 2025; n = 13,760), followed by risk-ratio, interrupted time-series, multivariable, age-stratified, co-detection, and sensitivity analyses.Children were categorized into four age groups: <1, 1–<3, 3–<6, and 6–14 years. This age stratification was selected according to commonly used pediatric respiratory infection epidemiology and the social contact patterns of children in China, broadly corresponding to infancy, early childhood mainly under home care, kindergarten age, and school age.2.3Respiratory pathogen testing and pathogen definitionsRespiratory pathogen nucleic acid testing was performed using a multiplex detection kit for 13 respiratory pathogens based on fluorescence PCR followed by capillary electrophoresis (PN: 1060071; Health GeneTech Co., Ltd., Ningbo, China). Nucleic acid extraction was performed using a TANBead SLA-32 automated nucleic acid extraction system. PCR amplification was performed using a SLAN-96P real-time PCR system. Amplification products were detected using an Applied Biosystems 3500 Dx Genetic Analyzer for capillary electrophoresis-based detection and fragment analysis. Sample processing, nucleic acid extraction, PCR amplification, capillary electrophoresis, quality control, and result interpretation were performed according to the manufacturer's instructions and local standard operating procedures.The main analysis included 13 respiratory pathogen categories: influenza A virus not further classified by this panel (InfA-NFC), influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, seasonal influenza A (H3N2) virus, influenza B virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, human parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, human rhinovirus, human adenovirus, seasonal human coronaviruses, human bocavirus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and Chlamydia spp. In this study, InfA-NFC referred to records positive for the manufacturer-reported generic influenza A target, listed as InfA in the manufacturer's instructions, but not classified as influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus or seasonal influenza A (H3N2) virus. The seasonal human coronaviruses category did not include SARS-CoV-2. Throughout the study period, SARS-CoV-2 testing, when clinically indicated, was performed through a separate dedicated nucleic acid testing pathway and was therefore not included in the fixed 13-target respiratory pathogen panel analyzed in this study. The Chlamydia category was not further differentiated into C. trachomatis or C. pneumoniae. Pathogen abbreviations, full pathogen names, manufacturer-reported detection targets, and limits of detection are provided in Supplementary Table S1.A composite influenza A variable was defined as positivity for any influenza A-related analytic category, including InfA-NFC, influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, or seasonal influenza A(H3N2) virus. This composite variable was used only for descriptive summaries and was not included as an additional category in the main risk ratio, multiple-comparison, interrupted time-series, or multivariable regression analyses to avoid double counting. Overall positivity was defined as positivity for at least one of the 13 main respiratory pathogen categories. Co-detection was defined as positivity for two or more of the 13 main pathogen categories in the same testing record. Positivity and co-detection rates were calculated using the corresponding number of testing records as the denominator. A 13-target-negative record was defined as a testing record in which none of the 13 main respiratory pathogen categories was detected. Overall positivity and 13-target-negative proportions describe laboratory detection among tested pediatric and neonatal inpatients and were not intended as estimates of community incidence or prevalence.2.4Study periods, seasons, and school-term statusThe study period was divided according to the timing of COVID-19 policy adjustment in China and the monthly structure of the dataset. January 2021 to December 2022 was defined as the NPI period, and January 2023 to December 2025 was defined as the post-NPI period. In interrupted time-series analyses, January 2023 was treated as the first post-intervention month. Seasons were defined by calendar month: spring, March to May; summer, June to August; autumn, September to November; and winter, December to February. School-term status was defined at the calendar-day level according to the official local school calendar rather than by calendar month alone and assigned to each testing record based on the application date. Each testing record was classified as occurring during an in-school term or a vacation period. This variable was used as a population-level contextual indicator of periods with increased or decreased community contact networks related to kindergarten and school attendance.2.5Meteorological and air-quality dataDaily meteorological observations for Nanchong, Sichuan Province, China were obtained from RP5 (Reliable Prognosis), a publicly available weather data platform providing observational data from ground weather stations. Daily air quality index (AQI) records were obtained from the 2345 Weather historical weather database for Nanchong, a publicly accessible weather and air-quality information platform that provides city-level historical weather records with daily air-quality information (https://tianqi.2345.com/wea_history/57411.htm; accessed July 4, 2026). Before monthly aggregation, extracted AQI records were checked for completeness, date consistency, plausible value ranges, and temporal continuity. Daily temperature, relative humidity, and AQI records were aggregated into monthly means for each calendar month and linked to individual testing records by year-month. Temperature was modeled per 1 °C increase, relative humidity per 10% increase, and AQI per 10-unit increase. Meteorological and AQI variables were available for all 60 calendar months from January 2021 to December 2025 and were matched to the testing dataset by year-month.2.6Statistical analysisAll statistical analyses were based on the final analytic dataset of 20,250 testing records. Categorical variables were summarized as counts and percentages. Continuous variables were summarized as medians with interquartile ranges or means with standard deviations, as appropriate. All tests were two-sided, and P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. For multiple comparisons across the 13 main pathogen categories, the Benjamini–Hochberg method was used to control the false discovery rate (FDR). All statistical analyses were performed using Python software. Data management and aggregation were conducted using pandas and NumPy. Statistical calculations and modeling were performed using SciPy and statsmodels, and figures were generated using matplotlib.2.6.1Baseline characteristics and period comparisonsBaseline characteristics and pathogen detection profiles were compared between the NPI and post-NPI periods. Categorical variables were compared using the χ2 test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Continuous variables were compared using the Mann–Whitney U test or t test, depending on distributional characteristics. The composite influenza A variable was presented only as a descriptive summary, with influenza A subtypes listed separately. Continuous age is presented as median (interquartile range) and was compared between the NPI and post-NPI periods using the Mann–Whitney U test.2.6.2Risk ratio analysisDetection risks for the 13 main respiratory pathogen categories were compared between the NPI and post-NPI periods. For each pathogen, positivity rates were calculated for both periods, and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. FDR-adjusted P values were used to assess statistical robustness under multiple testing. As an additional RSV-focused supplementary analysis, age was reclassified into clinically relevant categories for RSV burden and prevention strategies. RSV detection was first compared between children aged <2 years and those aged ≥2 years. Children were further categorized as 0–<6 months, 6–<12 months, 12–<24 months, and ≥24 months. For each category, RSV positivity was summarized for the NPI and post-NPI periods, and post-NPI vs. NPI risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), P values, and FDR-adjusted P values were calculated. This RSV-specific supplementary analysis was designed to provide clinical and public-health detail for the age windows most relevant to infant and toddler RSV prevention.2.6.3Interrupted time-series analysisTo evaluate whether the period difference in overall positivity could reflect a general long-term trend, monthly overall positivity was first analyzed using a single time-trend model without an interruption term. A segmented interrupted time-series model was then fitted using January 2023 as the first post-interruption month, corresponding to the January 8, 2023 policy transition, to estimate the pre-interruption trend, immediate level change, and post-interruption trend change. A joint Wald test evaluated the combined evidence for the immediate level and trend changes, and a grouped binomial model based on monthly positive and negative counts was used as a sensitivity analysis.Interrupted time-series (ITS) segmented regression models were used to assess immediate level changes and post-intervention trend changes in monthly pathogen positivity after the lifting of NPIs. ITS and segmented regression models are commonly used to evaluate level and slope changes after public health policy or intervention changes (21–24).For each pathogen, the monthly positivity rate was used as the outcome. The core independent variables included time, intervention status, and time after intervention. Month fixed effects were included to account for seasonality. Models were weighted by the monthly number of testing records. Newey–West robust standard errors were used to account for potential autocorrelation (25). The primary model used Newey–West lag = 1, and lag = 3 was used as a sensitivity analysis.The model was specified as: Yt = β0 + β1 × time + β2 × intervention + β3 × post-intervention time + month fixed effects + εt, where β1 represents the pre-intervention monthly trend, β2 represents the immediate level change after the lifting of NPIs, and β3 represents the post-intervention trend change.2.6.4Multivariable logistic regressionTo evaluate factors associated with pathogen positivity, separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for each of the 13 main respiratory pathogen categories. The core independent variables were monthly mean temperature, monthly mean relative humidity, monthly mean AQI, and school-term status. Models were adjusted for age group, sex, and pandemic phase. Because meteorological exposures, seasonality, and time trends may be correlated, season was not included in the primary model to reduce potential collinearity; this approach was consistent with general considerations in environmental time-series modeling (26). Cluster-robust standard errors were estimated at the year-month level. Results were reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% CIs. To assess whether environmental and temporal associations differed between the NPI and post-NPI periods, separate interaction models were fitted by adding temperature × phase, relative humidity × phase, AQI × phase, and school term × phase terms to the pathogen-specific multivariable models. Across 13 pathogen categories and four contextual factors, 52 interaction tests were prespecified. full_text_sections.abstract: BackgroundCOVID-19-related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) disrupted the circulation of many respiratory pathogens. After these measures were lifted, pediatric respiratory pathogen activity may have changed in pathogen-specific ways. However, laboratory-based evidence using continuous multi-year data, interrupted time-series analysis, and contextual factors such as meteorology, air quality, and school calendars remains limited.MethodsWe conducted a single-center retrospective laboratory study of pediatric and neonatal inpatients aged 0–14 years with clinically diagnosed lower respiratory tract infection from January 2021 to December 2025. After 7-day deduplication within the same child, 20,250 throat-swab testing records were included. The NPI period was January 2021–December 2022, and the post-NPI period was January 2023–December 2025. Thirteen pathogen categories were analyzed using period comparisons, interrupted time-series models, and multivariable logistic regression incorporating meteorological factors, air quality index, and school-term status.ResultsOverall positivity was higher in the post-NPI period than in the NPI period (75.4% vs. 58.8%), and co-detection was also higher in the post-NPI period (15.2% vs. 6.0%). Pathogen-specific interrupted time-series analysis showed heterogeneous patterns: human adenovirus showed a robust immediate level decrease (−13.00 percentage points; 95% CI, −20.13 to −5.87; FDR-adjusted P = 0.005), whereas human rhinovirus showed a significant positive trend change after the January 2023 interruption (+1.07 percentage points per month; 95% CI, 0.63–1.50; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001), with a positive post-NPI slope (+0.64 percentage points per month). Higher temperature was associated with lower positivity of human respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, and influenza B virus, but higher positivity of human parainfluenza virus and human bocavirus. School-term status was associated with higher human rhinovirus positivity (aOR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.34–2.52; FDR-adjusted P = 0.002).ConclusionThe NPI and post-NPI periods showed distinct and heterogeneous temporal patterns in pediatric respiratory pathogen detection. These findings support integrated hospital-based laboratory surveillance centered on pathogen-specific temporal trends and interpreted alongside demographic, multi-pathogen, environmental, school-calendar, and longer-term temporal context.
full_text_sections.methods: 2Materials and methods2.1Study design, setting, and data sourceThis single-center, laboratory-based retrospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Clinical Laboratory at Beijing Anzhen Nanchong Hospital of Capital Medical University and Nanchong Central Hospital, located in Nanchong, Sichuan Province, China. The hospital is a tertiary general hospital and clinical teaching hospital that receives patients from Nanchong and surrounding areas. Pediatric respiratory pathogen nucleic acid testing records from January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2025, were extracted from the laboratory information system. Throughout the study period, the data-collecting hospital, clinical laboratory, and respiratory pathogen testing framework remained consistent. Annual pediatric and neonatal inpatient volumes from 2021 to 2025 were obtained from hospital administrative records and used to calculate the number of respiratory pathogen testing records per 100 inpatient admissions as a contextual measure of testing volume across study periods.2.2Study populationEligible testing records were from pediatric or neonatal inpatients aged 0–14 years with a clinician-recorded diagnosis of lower respiratory tract infection on the laboratory test request. These patients underwent routine 13-target multiplex respiratory pathogen testing between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2025. Testing was ordered by clinicians according to the child's clinical presentation and diagnostic needs. Throat swabs were collected for respiratory pathogen nucleic acid testing. Records were required to contain complete information on sex, age, application date, and pathogen detection results. Outpatient and emergency department records were not included. Throughout the study period, the source wards, age range, eligibility criteria, and specimen type remained consistent.A total of 21,132 original identification records were initially available. After preliminary data cleaning, variable harmonization, and verification of key fields, 20,296 preliminary testing records were retained. To reduce the influence of repeated short-term testing from the same child, 7-day deduplication was performed using medical record numbers. For each child, testing records were ordered chronologically by application time; when multiple respiratory pathogen tests occurred within a 7-day window, only the first record was retained, whereas a test performed more than 7 days after the previously retained record was considered a new testing event. After deduplication, 46 short-term duplicate records were removed, leaving 20,250 testing records for the main analysis, including 6,490 records from the NPI period and 13,760 from the post-NPI period. The final dataset covered 60 consecutive months from January 2021 to December 2025. These were classified into the NPI period (January 2021-December 2022; n = 6,490) and post-NPI period (January 2023–December 2025; n = 13,760), followed by risk-ratio, interrupted time-series, multivariable, age-stratified, co-detection, and sensitivity analyses.Children were categorized into four age groups: <1, 1–<3, 3–<6, and 6–14 years. The seasonal human coronaviruses category did not include SARS-CoV-2. Throughout the study period, SARS-CoV-2 testing, when clinically indicated, was performed through a separate dedicated nucleic acid testing pathway and was therefore not included in the fixed 13-target respiratory pathogen panel analyzed in this study. The Chlamydia category was not further differentiated into C. trachomatis or C. pneumoniae. This composite variable was used only for descriptive summaries and was not included as an additional category in the main risk ratio, multiple-comparison, interrupted time-series, or multivariable regression analyses to avoid double counting. Overall positivity was defined as positivity for at least one of the 13 main respiratory pathogen categories. Co-detection was defined as positivity for two or more of the 13 main pathogen categories in the same testing record. Positivity and co-detection rates were calculated using the corresponding number of testing records as the denominator. A 13-target-negative record was defined as a testing record in which none of the 13 main respiratory pathogen categories was detected. full_text_sections.discussion: 4Discussion4.1Principal findingsThis 5-year hospital-based laboratory surveillance study identified marked changes in pediatric respiratory pathogen detection across the NPI and post-NPI periods, with distinct temporal patterns across pathogens. Overall positivity was higher in the post-NPI period than in the NPI period (75.4% vs. 58.8%), and co-detection was also more frequent (15.2% vs. 6.0%). At the aggregate level, overall positivity showed a significant long-term increasing trend over the 5-year study period, whereas segmented analysis using January 2023 as the interruption point showed no statistically significant immediate level or slope change. At the pathogen-specific level, ITS analyses revealed distinct temporal trajectories across pathogens, with human adenovirus showing a robust immediate decrease and human rhinovirus showing a significant positive trend change and a positive post-NPI slope. Associations with environmental factors and school-calendar status were likewise pathogen-specific, and phase-interaction analyses further showed that selected associations with temperature, relative humidity, and school-term status differed between the NPI and post-NPI periods. Overall, these findings demonstrate a complex temporal profile of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection characterized by a long-term aggregate trend, pathogen-specific changes, and associations with environmental and school-calendar factors.4.2Overall positivity, long-term trend, and co-detection across study periodsCOVID-19-related NPIs substantially altered the circulation of common respiratory pathogens (7–11), and subsequent studies reported renewed circulation and altered epidemiological patterns of multiple respiratory pathogens following relaxation of these measures (12–16). In our study, overall positivity was higher in the post-NPI period than in the NPI period. Further analysis of the overall temporal trend showed that overall positivity increased by an average of 0.49 percentage points per month over the 5-year study period, whereas segmented analysis with January 2023 as the interruption point did not show significant changes in the overall level or trend. These findings place the higher overall positivity observed in the post-NPI period within a broader long-term upward trend and suggest that aggregate measures may not fully capture heterogeneous temporal dynamics across individual pathogens.Co-detection also increased markedly in the post-NPI period, and this increase was supported by both the period comparison and weighted ITS analysis. This pattern may reflect greater temporal overlap in the circulation of multiple respiratory pathogens, thereby increasing the likelihood of detecting more than one pathogen in the same specimen. For hospital-based laboratory surveillance, co-detection patterns provide information beyond single-pathogen positivity and add complexity to etiological attribution and laboratory interpretation. Accordingly, considering both single-pathogen temporal trends and multi-pathogen co-detection patterns may provide a more complete characterization of pediatric respiratory pathogen activity in the post-NPI period.4.3Pathogen-specific reshaping of detection patternsA central finding of this study is that pathogen detection patterns changed heterogeneously after the lifting of NPIs. Although many pathogen categories showed higher detection risks in the post-NPI period, the magnitude, timing, and stability of changes varied across pathogens. This pattern is consistent with reports of asynchronous respiratory virus resurgence and pathogen-specific recovery after relaxation of COVID-19-related restrictions (12, 14, 30). It supports the concept that the post-NPI period may represent pathogen-specific reshaping rather than a simple synchronized return to pre-pandemic seasonality. This distinction is important because aggregate respiratory pathogen positivity may obscure divergent trajectories among individual pathogens.Human rhinovirus showed the most statistically robust trend-related finding in our ITS analysis, with a significant positive trend change after the January 2023 interruption and a positive post-NPI slope. This pattern is consistent with previous pediatric studies showing that rhinovirus activity was less suppressed by NPIs and could remain prominent or increase while several other respiratory viruses showed marked reductions or altered circulation (31–33). The positive association between school-term status and human rhinovirus positivity across age strata is also consistent with evidence that school sessions, holidays, and closures can influence respiratory infection activity in children (20, 34, 35). Thus, human rhinovirus may function as a sensitive indicator of renewed pediatric contact networks in the post-NPI period. Nevertheless, school-term status in this study was defined by calendar timing and should be interpreted as a population-level contextual indicator rather than a direct measure of individual school attendance, classroom exposure, or transmission pathway.Several pathogens, including human metapneumovirus, influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, human parainfluenza virus, and seasonal human coronaviruses, showed immediate level increases in the primary ITS model. Similar post-restriction shifts in human metapneumovirus, influenza, and other respiratory viruses have been reported after periods of reduced circulation or relaxation of COVID-19 restrictions (13, 36, 37). However, these signals in our study were attenuated after FDR correction, indicating lower statistical robustness under multiple-comparison control. These findings are still informative because they suggest transient post-NPI increases for several pathogens, while also showing that not all apparent rebounds were statistically stable after adjustment for multiple testing. For influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, the large period-comparison RR and wide confidence interval mainly reflected sparse detections during the NPI period, indicating a marked post-NPI increase with limited precision of the RR estimate.The RSV-focused supplementary analysis further highlights the translational relevance of age-specific surveillance, consistent with previous evidence that RSV contributes substantially to acute lower respiratory infection burden in young children and that RSV activity was altered during and after COVID-19-related restriction periods (2, 10–12). Although the primary age strata were designed to reflect childcare and schooling stages in China, reclassification into RSV prevention-relevant age windows showed that children younger than 2 years accounted for most RSV-positive records and had nearly twice the overall RSV detection risk observed in older children. The highest positivity was observed in the 6–<12-month and 12–<24-month groups, supporting the importance of infant- and toddler-focused RSV prevention and surveillance strategies. The stronger relative post-NPI increase among children aged ≥2 years also suggests broader age redistribution of RSV detection after the lifting of NPIs. Because this study was based on laboratory testing records, these findings should be interpreted as age-specific RSV detection patterns in a laboratory surveillance dataset and may inform future studies that link virological detection with hospitalization and severity outcomes.Human adenovirus showed a contrasting pattern, with both a lower post-NPI detection risk and a robust immediate level decrease in ITS analysis. This divergence from HRV further highlights the pathogen-specific nature of post-NPI changes. This pattern underscores the value of local pathogen-specific laboratory surveillance, because decreases in selected pathogens may be hidden when respiratory pathogen activity is assessed only through aggregate positivity. full_text_sections.conclusion: 5ConclusionOver 5 years of continuous hospital-based laboratory surveillance, pediatric respiratory pathogen detection showed distinct overall and pathogen-specific patterns across the NPI and post-NPI periods, with higher overall positivity and co-detection rates in the post-NPI period. Pathogen-specific interrupted time-series analyses further revealed different temporal trajectories, including an immediate decrease in HADV and a significant positive trend change in HRV with a positive post-NPI slope. Age-stratified analyses and assessments of meteorological and school-calendar factors further showed that associations between pathogen detection, age, and contextual factors were pathogen-specific; phase-interaction analyses additionally indicated that the associations of temperature with HPIV, school-term status with H3, and relative humidity with Ch differed between the NPI and post-NPI periods. Taken together, these findings support continued hospital-based multi-pathogen laboratory surveillance integrating pathogen-specific temporal trends, age stratification, co-detection patterns, and environmental and school-calendar context to facilitate dynamic identification of pediatric respiratory pathogen activity, prioritization of surveillance targets, and pediatric service preparedness.
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionAcute respiratory infections remain a major cause of illness among children worldwide and are associated with substantial healthcare use, hospitalization, and public health burden (1). Among specific pediatric pathogens, respiratory syncytial virus, seasonal influenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and human parainfluenza virus contribute substantially to acute lower respiratory infection burden in young children (2–5). Laboratory-based surveillance in China has also shown that pediatric and community respiratory specimens can involve diverse viral and atypical pathogens rather than a single dominant target (6). These patterns vary by age, season, geography, and social contact structure, highlighting the importance of continuous laboratory-based surveillance for understanding temporal changes in pediatric respiratory pathogen activity.During the COVID-19 pandemic, non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), such as mask wearing, school closures, reduced mobility, physical distancing, and enhanced hygiene measures, substantially altered community respiratory virus activity beyond SARS-CoV-2 (7). Observational and pediatric hospital-based studies in China showed broad impacts of NPIs on acute respiratory infections and common childhood respiratory viruses (8, 9). Respiratory syncytial virus-specific studies also reported altered epidemiological and clinical characteristics among hospitalized children during the pandemic period (10). Studies have described off-season or asynchronous resurgence of influenza viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, human metapneumovirus, and other common respiratory viruses after periods of reduced activity (11–13). Post-NPI resurgence or shifting epidemic features of Mycoplasma pneumoniae have also been reported in China and related pediatric studies (14, 15). The concept of immune debt has further been proposed to help explain heterogeneous pediatric respiratory infection activity after the pandemic (16). These observations suggest that the post-NPI period may be better understood as a phase of pathogen-specific reshaping of respiratory pathogen detection patterns rather than a simple return to pre-pandemic seasonality.In parallel with changes in population contact patterns, environmental and calendar-related factors may provide important context for respiratory pathogen activity. Temperature and meteorological conditions have been associated with viral seasonality and pathogen-specific acute respiratory infection patterns (17, 18). Air pollution has also been linked to respiratory infection susceptibility and pediatric respiratory health (19). School sessions have been associated with seasonal outbreaks of medically attended respiratory infections (20). Nevertheless, few studies have jointly evaluated meteorological conditions, air quality, and school-term status across multiple pediatric respiratory pathogen categories in the post-NPI period.Although evidence on post-NPI respiratory pathogen activity is increasing, the available literature remains constrained by several methodological limitations. papers.title_original: Ecological reshaping of pediatric respiratory pathogen profiles after COVID-19-related non-pharmaceutical interventions were lifted: a 5-year interrupted time-series study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how the lifting of non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) related to COVID-19 affected the ecological patterns of pediatric respiratory pathogens, particularly human adenoviruses, over a 5-year period.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This interrupted time-series study analyzed pediatric respiratory pathogen testing records from a tertiary general hospital and clinical teaching hospital in Nanchong, China, between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2025. A total of 20,250 throat-swab testing records were included after 7-day deduplication within the same child.
analysis.methods: The study used 13-target multiplex respiratory pathogen testing, extracting nucleic acid testing records from the hospital's laboratory information system. Data were collected consistently throughout the study period, and analyses included period comparisons, interrupted time-series models, and multivariable logistic regression incorporating meteorological factors, air quality index, and school-term status.
analysis.main_results: Overall positivity was higher in the post-NPI period than in the NPI period (75.4% vs. 58.8%), and co-detection was also higher (15.2% vs. Human adenovirus showed a robust immediate level decrease (−13.00 percentage points; 95% CI, −20.13 to −5.87; FDR-adjusted P = 0.005), whereas human rhinovirus showed a significant positive trend change after the January 2023 interruption (+1.07 percentage points per month; 95% CI, 0.63–1.50; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001), with a positive post-NPI slope (+0.64 percentage points per month).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the lifting of NPIs led to complex changes in pediatric respiratory pathogen detection, including a significant immediate decrease in human adenovirus and a positive trend change in human rhinovirus, highlighting the pathogen-specific effects of environmental and behavioral factors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that changes in public health measures can significantly alter the epidemiological patterns of respiratory pathogens, which has implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and understanding the dynamics of pediatric respiratory diseases in post-pandemic settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on hospital-based data, which may not represent the broader population. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on observational data and statistical models rather than experimental interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This 5-year interrupted time-series study investigated the impact of lifting non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) related to COVID-19 on pediatric respiratory pathogen profiles, focusing on human adenoviruses. The study analyzed nucleic acid testing records from a tertiary hospital in Nanchong, China, and found that overall positivity and co-detection rates increased in the post-NPI period. Human adenovirus showed a significant immediate decrease, while human rhinovirus exhibited a positive trend change. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of complex ecological shifts in respiratory pathogen circulation, influenced by environmental and school-related factors. The study's reliance on hospital data and statistical models limits the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate. These results have implications for understanding how public health measures affect respiratory disease patterns and for improving surveillance and diagnostic strategies in post-pandemic contexts.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,NPI 的取消导致了儿科呼吸道病原体检测的复杂变化,包括 人腺病毒 的立即显着下降和人类鼻病毒的积极趋势变化,突出了环境和行为因素对病原体的特异性影响。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖医院数据而受到限制,这些数据可能无法代表更广泛的人群。证据是中等的,因为结果是基于观察数据和统计模型而不是实验干预。

人腺病毒4型(HAdV-4)是引起急性呼吸道感染的主要血清型之一,目前尚无获批临床应用的抗体药物,存在迫切的未满足医疗需求。本研究旨在通过解析感染后的B细胞免疫应答,鉴定高效的中和抗体,从而为疫苗设计与抗病毒治疗奠定基础。研究人员从16名HAdV-4康复志愿者中筛选出其中和抗体滴度最高的个体,分离其外周血单个核细胞(PBMCs)。共从该患者外周血中分选获得2710个B细胞,并通过整合单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)与单细胞VDJ测序(scVDJ-seq)技术,全面分析了B细胞亚群特征及B细胞受体(BCR)库。随后,基于BCR特征及其来源,筛选候选抗体进行一系列功能与机制验证。转录组分析将记忆B细胞分为三个功能异质性亚群,分别命名为MB sub1、sub2与sub3。结合BCR特征,研究人员从sub2与sub3中选取92个抗体进行合成及进一步功能验证。成功鉴定出三株高效中和抗体,其中1QH7在体外展现出强效病毒中和能力,并在Stat1基因缺陷小鼠模型中提供显著的体内保护效果。研究人员进一步利用AlphaFold 3预测了1QH7与HAdV-4六邻体蛋白(Hexon protein)的复合物结构,并通过定点诱变验证了关键结合残基。此外,研究阐明了由TRIM21介导的病毒中和机制。本研究建立了一种基于scRNA-seq与scVDJ-seq整合分析的高效抗体筛选策略,并分离出一株高效中和抗体1QH7,为新型突发传染病暴发时快速开展非病原体诱饵依赖、细胞亚群引导的抗体筛选路径奠定了坚实基础。 研究背景与意义 欢迎领取《放射性同位素检测一站式解决方案》领 取 人腺病毒4型(HAdV-4)是一种全球流行的呼吸道病原体,是引起急性呼吸道感染的主要血清型之一。婴幼儿、儿童及免疫功能低下者更易感,部分病例可进展为重症肺炎甚至死亡。近年来,HAdV-4在普通社区人群中的检出率显著上升。一项来自广州儿童医院的回顾性研究显示,在1988年至2005年间死于肺炎的儿童肺组织样本中,HAdV-4占所有腺病毒阳性病例的比例高达75%,提示其可能是导致儿童致死性肺炎的关键血清型。然而,目前尚缺乏针对HAdV-4的特异性抗病毒药物及获批用于普通人群的疫苗,临床治疗仍以支持性护理为主。因此,开发高效安全的特异性抗病毒策略是一项迫切且未满足的临床需求。 传统中和抗体筛选方法通量低、耗时长,依赖对大量克隆的逐一验证,通常需要数月时间,难以应对新型或突发传染病的快速响应。单细胞测序技术的突破性进展为高效抗体筛选提供了新的解决方案。基于微流控平台,单细胞测序技术能够高通量并行捕获数万个单个B细胞的转录组和VDJ序列,实现自动化BCR配对,将抗体发现周期从数月缩短至数天。当与生物信息学深度挖掘B细胞库多样性相结合时,可为快速锁定具有特定表达特征或突变模式的候选抗体提供强大工具。 本研究旨在建立一种整合单细胞测序与功能验证的抗体发现策略,从HAdV-4康复供体中鉴定高效中和抗体,为疫苗设计和抗病毒治疗奠定基础,同时验证基于单细胞测序的抗体发现平台在新发传染病应对中的效率与适用性。 主要关键技术方法 研究人员从16名HAdV-4康复志愿者中筛选出中和抗体滴度最高的供体,分离其外周血单个核细胞(PBMCs),经流式细胞术分选出2710个B细胞。采用10x Genomics平台的单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)与单细胞VDJ测序(scVDJ-seq)技术,同步获取B细胞的转录组与BCR序列信息。通过整合分析,对B细胞亚群进行分类与注释,并基于BCR的V-J基因组合特征及体细胞高频突变(SHM)水平,从记忆B细胞亚群中筛选候选抗体进行合成与功能验证。体内保护实验采用Stat1基因缺陷小鼠模型进行攻毒实验。抗原-抗体复合物结构通过AlphaFold 3进行预测,并结合定点诱变进行关键结合残基验证。 研究结果 2.1 单细胞转录组图谱揭示B细胞异质性景观 研究人员通过无监督聚类和细胞类型注释,将2710个B细胞划分为11个细胞簇,包括初始B细胞(25.35%)、浆细胞(23.28%)、记忆B细胞(47.08%)及其他细胞(4.28%)。记忆B细胞被进一步分为三个转录组学上不同的亚群:MB sub1(44.28%)、MB sub2(22.49%)和MB sub3(33.23%)。差异表达基因分析和基因本体论(GO)富集分析显示,三个亚群功能各异:MB sub1可能主要参与免疫监视;MB sub2代表中间或过渡状态,可能在免疫调节中发挥作用;MB sub3则准备分化为浆细胞,主要参与抗体分泌的准备。伪时间轨迹分析进一步证实了这一分化顺序,MB sub1分布于初始分支段,而sub2和sub3位于终末分支段。 2.2 不同B细胞群体中BCR免疫库的特征 研究人员鉴定了1972个全长配对BCR。浆细胞主要表达IGHM(97.62%),而记忆B细胞同时表达IGHA(27.74%)、IGHM(30.25%)和IGHG(31.66%)。三个记忆B细胞亚群表现出不同的抗体同种型表达谱:MB sub1主要表达IGHM,而MB sub2和sub3主要表达IGHG。MB sub2和sub3的SHM水平显著高于MB sub1,且MB sub2的CDR3长度显著长于MB sub1和MB sub3。BCR多样性分析显示,MB sub2的香农指数显著高于MB sub1,表明sub2可能含有sub1和sub3中缺失的稀有克隆。这些结果表明MB sub2更可能包含通过亲和成熟富集的高亲和力抗体。 2.3 中和抗体在记忆B细胞亚群中的定位 研究人员依据MB sub2或sub3中CDR长度或SHM水平高于sub1的标准,选择了特定的重链V-J基因组合,合成了源自MB sub2和sub3的92个抗体序列。酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)鉴定出5株对六邻体蛋白(Hexon)具有高结合活性的单克隆抗体,EC50值均低于30 ng/mL。假病毒中和试验显示,1QH7、1AG5和3WS9三株抗体具有强效中和活性,IC50值均低于50 ng/mL,其中1QH7最为强效(IC50=5.31 ng/mL)。真实病毒中和试验进一步确认了1QH7对HAdV-4的中和能力。竞争ELISA和AlphaFold 3预测的结构模型表明,这三株抗体结合六邻体蛋白的不同区域。表面等离子共振(SPR)测定显示1QH7与六邻体蛋白具有高亲和力结合(KD=5.88 nM)。差示扫描量热法(DSC)显示其具有良好的结构稳定性。1QH7对HAdV-5和HAdV-7无交叉中和活性,证实其严格的血清型特异性。 2.4 1QH7在Stat1缺陷小鼠模型中保护免受HAdV-4攻击 在Stat1基因缺陷小鼠模型中,预防性给予1QH7(2 μg、10 μg或50 μg)24小时后进行攻毒,结果显示剂量依赖性地提高了生存率和体重恢复。10 μg剂量在预防和治疗方案中均提供完全保护。攻毒后3天收集的组织病毒载量分析显示,预防组和治疗组的肺和肝脏病毒拷贝数均显著低于病毒对照组。病理学检查显示,抗体处理组的肺部损伤明显减轻,平均综合病理评分显著低于病毒对照组。 2.5 TRIM21介导的细胞内1QH7中和机制 共聚焦显微镜观察显示,内化的抗体-病毒复合物与内源性TRIM21存在显著共定位。在TRIM21敲低或过表达的细胞中进行假病毒中和试验,结果显示TRIM21敲低减弱了抗体介导的中和作用,而TRIM21过表达增强了这一活性。进一步的共定位分析显示,K48连接的泛素链被特异性招募到抗体-病毒复合物上。此外,使用泛素化通路抑制剂显著降低了抗体的中和活性。这些结果表明,1QH7进入细胞后被胞质受体TRIM21识别,可能通过招募K48连接泛素化系统,以泛素-蛋白酶体依赖性方式促进病毒颗粒的细胞内清除。 讨论与结论 本研究建立了一种整合单细胞测序框架,以解析针对HAdV-4感染的B细胞免疫应答。通过结合scRNA-seq和scVDJ-seq,研究人员成功以空前分辨率表征了B细胞的转录组和BCR库景观。分析不仅揭示了感染恢复后B细胞组成的变化,还识别出功能特化的记忆B细胞亚群,其中MB sub2和sub3亚群显示出与潜在中和抗体产生相关的转录特征。基于这些发现,研究人员合成了该亚群中富集的特定V-J基因组合对应的92个抗体进行表达和筛选,成功鉴定出三株中和抗体。其中,单克隆抗体1QH7在细胞和动物模型中均展现出强效中和活性。进一步整合抗原-抗体结构分析和基于共聚焦显微镜的细胞内中和共定位研究,为其作用机制提供了初步见解。此外,另外两株中和抗体可用于开发联合疗法或双特异性抗体,为未来治疗策略提供更多选择。 本研究证明,单细胞整合技术在抗体发现中具有高效性。然而,也存在一些局限性:流式细胞术分选B细胞的策略可能偏向表面BCR高表达的亚群;对单一供体的关注限制了关于胚系基因使用偏好的结论普适性。扩大供体样本量将有助于识别与中和广度相关的保守BCR特征,并推动广谱抗体的开发。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! sub1、sub2与sub3。结合BCR特征,研究人员从sub2与sub3中选取92个抗体进行合成及进一步功能验证。成功鉴定出三株高效中和抗体,其中1QH7在体外展现出强效病毒中和能力,并在Stat1基因缺陷小鼠模型中提供显著的体内保护效果。研究人员进一步利用AlphaFold 3预测了1QH7与HAdV-4六邻体蛋白(Hexon protein)的复合物结构,并通过定点诱变验证了关键结合残基。此外,研究阐明了由TRIM21介导的病毒中和机制。本研究建立了一种基于scRNA-seq与scVDJ-seq整合分析的高效抗体筛选策略,并分离出一株高效中和抗体1QH7,为新型突发传染病暴发时快速开展非病原体诱饵依赖、细胞亚群引导的抗体筛选路径奠定了坚实基础。 研究背景与意义 欢迎领取《放射性同位素检测一站式解决方案》领 取 人腺病毒4型(HAdV-4)是一种全球流行的呼吸道病原体,是引起急性呼吸道感染的主要血清型之一。婴幼儿、儿童及免疫功能低下者更易感,部分病例可进展为重症肺炎甚至死亡。近年来,HAdV-4在普通社区人群中的检出率显著上升。一项来自广州儿童医院的回顾性研究显示,在1988年至2005年间死于肺炎的儿童肺组织样本中,HAdV-4占所有腺病毒阳性病例的比例高达75%,提示其可能是导致儿童致死性肺炎的关键血清型。然而,目前尚缺乏针对HAdV-4的特异性抗病毒药物及获批用于普通人群的疫苗,临床治疗仍以支持性护理为主。因此,开发高效安全的特异性抗病毒策略是一项迫切且未满足的临床需求。 传统中和抗体筛选方法通量低、耗时长,依赖对大量克隆的逐一验证,通常需要数月时间,难以应对新型或突发传染病的快速响应。单细胞测序技术的突破性进展为高效抗体筛选提供了新的解决方案。基于微流控平台,单细胞测序技术能够高通量并行捕获数万个单个B细胞的转录组和VDJ序列,实现自动化BCR配对,将抗体发现周期从数月缩短至数天。当与生物信息学深度挖掘B细胞库多样性相结合时,可为快速锁定具有特定表达特征或突变模式的候选抗体提供强大工具。 本研究旨在建立一种整合单细胞测序与功能验证的抗体发现策略,从HAdV-4康复供体中鉴定高效中和抗体,为疫苗设计和抗病毒治疗奠定基础,同时验证基于单细胞测序的抗体发现平台在新发传染病应对中的效率与适用性。 主要关键技术方法 研究人员从16名HAdV-4康复志愿者中筛选出中和抗体滴度最高的供体,分离其外周血单个核细胞(PBMCs),经流式细胞术分选出2710个B细胞。采用10x Genomics平台的单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)与单细胞VDJ测序(scVDJ-seq)技术,同步获取B细胞的转录组与BCR序列信息。通过整合分析,对B细胞亚群进行分类与注释,并基于BCR的V-J基因组合特征及体细胞高频突变(SHM)水平,从记忆B细胞亚群中筛选候选抗体进行合成与功能验证。体内保护实验采用Stat1基因缺陷小鼠模型进行攻毒实验。抗原-抗体复合物结构通过AlphaFold 3进行预测,并结合定点诱变进行关键结合残基验证。 研究结果 2.1 单细胞转录组图谱揭示B细胞异质性景观 研究人员通过无监督聚类和细胞类型注释,将2710个B细胞划分为11个细胞簇,包括初始B细胞(25.35%)、浆细胞(23.28%)、记忆B细胞(47.08%)及其他细胞(4.28%)。记忆B细胞被进一步分为三个转录组学上不同的亚群:MB sub1(44.28%)、MB sub2(22.49%)和MB sub3(33.23%)。差异表达基因分析和基因本体论(GO)富集分析显示,三个亚群功能各异:MB sub1可能主要参与免疫监视;MB sub2代表中间或过渡状态,可能在免疫调节中发挥作用;MB sub3则准备分化为浆细胞,主要参与抗体分泌的准备。伪时间轨迹分析进一步证实了这一分化顺序,MB sub1分布于初始分支段,而sub2和sub3位于终末分支段。 2.2 不同B细胞群体中BCR免疫库的特征 研究人员鉴定了1972个全长配对BCR。浆细胞主要表达IGHM(97.62%),而记忆B细胞同时表达IGHA(27.74%)、IGHM(30.25%)和IGHG(31.66%)。三个记忆B细胞亚群表现出不同的抗体同种型表达谱:MB sub1主要表达IGHM,而MB sub2和sub3主要表达IGHG。MB sub2和sub3的SHM水平显著高于MB sub1,且MB sub2的CDR3长度显著长于MB sub1和MB sub3。BCR多样性分析显示,MB sub2的香农指数显著高于MB sub1,表明sub2可能含有sub1和sub3中缺失的稀有克隆。这些结果表明MB sub2更可能包含通过亲和成熟富集的高亲和力抗体。 2.3 中和抗体在记忆B细胞亚群中的定位 研究人员依据MB sub2或sub3中CDR长度或SHM水平高于sub1的标准,选择了特定的重链V-J基因组合,合成了源自MB sub2和sub3的92个抗体序列。酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)鉴定出5株对六邻体蛋白(Hexon)具有高结合活性的单克隆抗体,EC50值均低于30 ng/mL。假病毒中和试验显示,1QH7、1AG5和3WS9三株抗体具有强效中和活性,IC50值均低于50 ng/mL,其中1QH7最为强效(IC50=5.31 ng/mL)。真实病毒中和试验进一步确认了1QH7对HAdV-4的中和能力。竞争ELISA和AlphaFold 3预测的结构模型表明,这三株抗体结合六邻体蛋白的不同区域。表面等离子共振(SPR)测定显示1QH7与六邻体蛋白具有高亲和力结合(KD=5.88 nM)。差示扫描量热法(DSC)显示其具有良好的结构稳定性。1QH7对HAdV-5和HAdV-7无交叉中和活性,证实其严格的血清型特异性。 2.4 1QH7在Stat1缺陷小鼠模型中保护免受HAdV-4攻击 在Stat1基因缺陷小鼠模型中,预防性给予1QH7(2 μg、10 μg或50 μg)24小时后进行攻毒,结果显示剂量依赖性地提高了生存率和体重恢复。10 μg剂量在预防和治疗方案中均提供完全保护。攻毒后3天收集的组织病毒载量分析显示,预防组和治疗组的肺和肝脏病毒拷贝数均显著低于病毒对照组。病理学检查显示,抗体处理组的肺部损伤明显减轻,平均综合病理评分显著低于病毒对照组。 2.5 TRIM21介导的细胞内1QH7中和机制 共聚焦显微镜观察显示,内化的抗体-病毒复合物与内源性TRIM21存在显著共定位。在TRIM21敲低或过表达的细胞中进行假病毒中和试验,结果显示TRIM21敲低减弱了抗体介导的中和作用,而TRIM21过表达增强了这一活性。进一步的共定位分析显示,K48连接的泛素链被特异性招募到抗体-病毒复合物上。此外,使用泛素化通路抑制剂显著降低了抗体的中和活性。这些结果表明,1QH7进入细胞后被胞质受体TRIM21识别,可能通过招募K48连接泛素化系统,以泛素-蛋白酶体依赖性方式促进病毒颗粒的细胞内清除。 讨论与结论 本研究建立了一种整合单细胞测序框架,以解析针对HAdV-4感染的B细胞免疫应答。通过结合scRNA-seq和scVDJ-seq,研究人员成功以空前分辨率表征了B细胞的转录组和BCR库景观。分析不仅揭示了感染恢复后B细胞组成的变化,还识别出功能特化的记忆B细胞亚群,其中MB sub2和sub3亚群显示出与潜在中和抗体产生相关的转录特征。基于这些发现,研究人员合成了该亚群中富集的特定V-J基因组合对应的92个抗体进行表达和筛选,成功鉴定出三株中和抗体。其中,单克隆抗体1QH7在细胞和动物模型中均展现出强效中和活性。进一步整合抗原-抗体结构分析和基于共聚焦显微镜的细胞内中和共定位研究,为其作用机制提供了初步见解。此外,另外两株中和抗体可用于开发联合疗法或双特异性抗体,为未来治疗策略提供更多选择。 本研究证明,单细胞整合技术在抗体发现中具有高效性。然而,也存在一些局限性:流式细胞术分选B细胞的策略可能偏向表面BCR高表达的亚群;对单一供体的关注限制了关于胚系基因使用偏好的结论普适性。扩大供体样本量将有助于识别与中和广度相关的保守BCR特征,并推动广谱抗体的开发。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, October 5, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Adenovirus Types 3 and 7 Drive Winter Pneumonia Surge in Hospitalized Chinese Children by October 5, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Adenovirus Types 3 and 7 Drive Winter Pneumonia Surge in Hospitalized Chinese Children Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Human adenovirus has long been recognized as one of the most important viral causes of acute respiratory infections in children, yet its shifting genotype landscape at the regional level has remained poorly charted in many parts of China. A new three-year surveillance study from Tianjin, published in BMC Infectious Diseases, now provides one of the most detailed pictures to date of how this virus circulates among hospitalized children, which genetic types dominate, and how those types map onto different clinical outcomes. Drawing on nearly twenty thousand respiratory specimens collected between September 2022 and August 2025, the research team led by Yulian Fang and colleagues at Tianjin Children’s Hospital traced a dynamic epidemic in which one viral species displaced another as the dominant cause of pediatric respiratory disease. The scale of the analysis is one of its distinguishing strengths. The investigators tested 19,523 respiratory specimens from children admitted to the hospital with acute respiratory infections, screening each sample for human adenovirus using targeted next-generation sequencing, a technique that allows simultaneous detection and initial genetic typing of the virus. Overall, 1,704 samples tested positive, corresponding to a detection rate of 8.7 percent. That figure underscores how substantial a burden adenovirus places on pediatric inpatient services in the region, particularly given that the study period spanned three full respiratory seasons following the disruption of the COVID-19 pandemic years. Demographic patterns in the data were striking and statistically robust. Detection rates were significantly higher in boys than in girls, a difference the authors report with a P value of 0.002, and age proved to be an even stronger determinant of infection risk. Children between three and six years old showed the highest detection rate of any age group, at 11.9 percent, with significant heterogeneity across age strata overall. This preschool peak is consistent with the epidemiology of adenovirus in many settings, reflecting the combination of close contact in kindergartens and playgrounds, immature immune memory, and the high viral shedding that young children can sustain during respiratory illness. Beyond simply measuring how often the virus appeared, the team went on to determine which genotypes were responsible. From the positive samples, 1,447 could be successfully genotyped, and the analysis revealed 14 distinct genotypes belonging to five of the seven human adenovirus species, designated A, B, C, E, and F. Two types towered over the rest: HAdV-3 accounted for 51.5 percent of genotyped infections and HAdV-7 for 18.4 percent, followed by HAdV-1 at 12.2 percent, HAdV-2 at 6.6 percent, HAdV-21 at 6.3 percent, HAdV-5 at 2.4 percent, and HAdV-4 at 1.3 percent, with remaining genotypes making up the final 1.3 percent. To confirm the sequencing-based typing, the researchers randomly selected positive samples for conventional PCR amplification of the hexon gene, the principal surface protein-coding region used in adenovirus classification, and performed phylogenetic analysis against reference sequences from GenBank. Perhaps the most consequential finding is that genotype composition changed systematically with the age of the host. Preschool and school-aged children were infected mainly with HAdV-3 and HAdV-7, both members of species B, whereas infants and toddlers were predominantly infected with HAdV-3 and HAdV-1, the latter belonging to species C. The association between age group and genotype was highly significant, with a P value below 0.001. This age-stratified structure has practical implications: it suggests that the viruses circulating in daycare and school environments differ from those afflicting children in their first years of life, and that any vaccination or prevention strategy may need to account for these distinct transmission niches. Seasonality added another layer of structure to the epidemiology. Adenovirus was detected year-round, but the detection rate varied markedly by season, peaking in winter at 13.4 percent of tested specimens. The seasonal pattern intersected with genotype in an unexpected way. Species B viruses, particularly HAdV-3 and HAdV-7, dominated the winter months, while species C viruses, especially HAdV-1, were more commonly identified in summer. This genotype-season coupling, significant at P below 0.001, implies that winter respiratory disease admissions driven by adenovirus are not simply more frequent but also caused by a different set of viral types than summer cases, a nuance that could inform the timing of clinical preparedness and laboratory typing efforts. Temporal analysis across the three study years revealed an inter-annual shift in the viral population that may prove to be the study’s most cited observation. Before August 2023, species C adenoviruses were the predominant circulating group; after that point, species B took over as the dominant species. Such species-level turnover in a community setting is rarely documented with this level of resolution, and it raises questions about what ecological forces, whether waning population immunity, changes in contact patterns, or intrinsic viral fitness differences, drove the replacement. The authors’ data cannot answer that question definitively, but the documented shift provides a benchmark against which future surveillance in Tianjin and comparable regions can be measured. The clinical correlations are equally important for pediatric practice. The main diagnoses among adenovirus-positive children included pneumonia, bronchitis, tonsillopharyngitis, and upper respiratory tract infections. Genotype-phenotype association analysis showed that HAdV-3 and HAdV-7 were the predominant types in pneumonia cases, whereas HAdV-3 and HAdV-1 were more commonly associated with tonsillopharyngitis and upper respiratory tract infections. Most critically, children infected with HAdV-7 were significantly more likely to develop severe pneumonia, an association with a P value below 0.001. This finding aligns with the established reputation of HAdV-7 as the most virulent of the common respiratory adenovirus types and highlights why molecular typing of adenovirus in hospitalized children is not merely an academic exercise but can carry direct prognostic value at the bedside. For the study’s authors, the combined epidemiological, seasonal, and clinical picture supports a case for region-specific surveillance and targeted interventions. Because HAdV-3, HAdV-7, and HAdV-1 together accounted for the overwhelming majority of typed infections, they represent the logical priority targets for any multivalent vaccine formulated for this population. No licensed adenovirus vaccine is currently available for routine pediatric use in most countries, and existing military vaccines cover only types 4 and 7. The genotype distribution documented in Tianjin, with its clear dominance of type 3 and its age-specific and seasonal structure, offers exactly the kind of empirical evidence that vaccine developers and public health planners need when weighing which valences to include and how to prioritize rollout. The study also demonstrates the value of combining modern sequencing platforms with classical molecular methods. Targeted next-generation sequencing enabled high-throughput screening and typing across nearly twenty thousand specimens, while hexon gene PCR and phylogenetic analysis provided confirmatory genotyping anchored to international reference databases. The retrospective design, approved by the Ethics Committee of Tianjin Children’s Hospital with a waiver of written informed consent because de-identified residual specimens were used, allowed the team to assemble a dataset of unusual breadth without additional burden on patients. As respiratory virus surveillance becomes increasingly genomic in the post-pandemic era, this work illustrates how sustained, genotype-resolved monitoring of a single pathogen in a single pediatric population can reveal patterns, from species turnover to genotype-specific severity, that would be invisible to conventional diagnostic testing alone, and it establishes a detailed baseline for tracking how adenovirus evolution continues to shape childhood pneumonia in northern China. Perhaps the most consequential finding is that genotype composition changed systematically with the age of the host. Preschool and school-aged children were infected mainly with HAdV-3 and HAdV-7, both members of species B, whereas infants and toddlers were predominantly infected with HAdV-3 and HAdV-1, the latter belonging to species C. The association between age group and genotype was highly significant, with a P value below 0.001. This age-stratified structure has practical implications: it suggests that the viruses circulating in daycare and school environments differ from those afflicting children in their first years of life, and that any vaccination or prevention strategy may need to account for these distinct transmission niches. Seasonality added another layer of structure to the epidemiology. Adenovirus was detected year-round, but the detection rate varied markedly by season, peaking in winter at 13.4 percent of tested specimens. The seasonal pattern intersected with genotype in an unexpected way. Species B viruses, particularly HAdV-3 and HAdV-7, dominated the winter months, while species C viruses, especially HAdV-1, were more commonly identified in summer. This genotype-season coupling, significant at P below 0.001, implies that winter respiratory disease admissions driven by adenovirus are not simply more frequent but also caused by a different set of viral types than summer cases, a nuance that could inform the timing of clinical preparedness and laboratory typing efforts. Temporal analysis across the three study years revealed an inter-annual shift in the viral population that may prove to be the study’s most cited observation. Before August 2023, species C adenoviruses were the predominant circulating group; after that point, species B took over as the dominant species. Such species-level turnover in a community setting is rarely documented with this level of resolution, and it raises questions about what ecological forces, whether waning population immunity, changes in contact patterns, or intrinsic viral fitness differences, drove the replacement. The authors’ data cannot answer that question definitively, but the documented shift provides a benchmark against which future surveillance in Tianjin and comparable regions can be measured. The clinical correlations are equally important for pediatric practice. The main diagnoses among adenovirus-positive children included pneumonia, bronchitis, tonsillopharyngitis, and upper respiratory tract infections. Genotype-phenotype association analysis showed that HAdV-3 and HAdV-7 were the predominant types in pneumonia cases, whereas HAdV-3 and HAdV-1 were more commonly associated with tonsillopharyngitis and upper respiratory tract infections. Most critically, children infected with HAdV-7 were significantly more likely to develop severe pneumonia, an association with a P value below 0.001. This finding aligns with the established reputation of HAdV-7 as the most virulent of the common respiratory adenovirus types and highlights why molecular typing of adenovirus in hospitalized children is not merely an academic exercise but can carry direct prognostic value at the bedside. For the study’s authors, the combined epidemiological, seasonal, and clinical picture supports a case for region-specific surveillance and targeted interventions. Because HAdV-3, HAdV-7, and HAdV-1 together accounted for the overwhelming majority of typed infections, they represent the logical priority targets for any multivalent vaccine formulated for this population. No licensed adenovirus vaccine is currently available for routine pediatric use in most countries, and existing military vaccines cover only types 4 and 7. The genotype distribution documented in Tianjin, with its clear dominance of type 3 and its age-specific and seasonal structure, offers exactly the kind of empirical evidence that vaccine developers and public health planners need when weighing which valences to include and how to prioritize rollout. The study also demonstrates the value of combining modern sequencing platforms with classical molecular methods. Targeted next-generation sequencing enabled high-throughput screening and typing across nearly twenty thousand specimens, while hexon gene PCR and phylogenetic analysis provided confirmatory genotyping anchored to international reference databases. The retrospective design, approved by the Ethics Committee of Tianjin Children’s Hospital with a waiver of written informed consent because de-identified residual specimens were used, allowed the team to assemble a dataset of unusual breadth without additional burden on patients. As respiratory virus surveillance becomes increasingly genomic in the post-pandemic era, this work illustrates how sustained, genotype-resolved monitoring of a single pathogen in a single pediatric population can reveal patterns, from species turnover to genotype-specific severity, that would be invisible to conventional diagnostic testing alone, and it establishes a detailed baseline for tracking how adenovirus evolution continues to shape childhood pneumonia in northern China.
